summary: Regime read: Tightening. Of the weighted evidence, 77% points tightening, 15% mixed, and 8% easing. Inflation is strongly tightening (per Federal Reserve: Summary of Economic Projections, September 16, 2026). Fed communications are strongly tightening (per StockTitan: Fed rate hike Sept 16, 2026: 3.75%-4.00%, One More Coming). Employment is strongly easing and market pricing is strongly tightening.
what_would_change_the_call: A second consecutive upside inflation surprise.
Front-end (2Y) yields rising materially further over the intermeeting window.
A Fed official explicitly pushing back against near-term cuts.
Fed funds futures repricing from 'fewer cuts' toward outright hikes.

checklist.text: Fed communications explicitly de-emphasize further easing
Fed emphasizes inflation upside risks over labor weakness
Market pricing removes expected cuts or starts pricing hikes
2Y yields rise materially over the intermeeting window
Inflation data surprises to the upside
Employment remains firm enough to reduce pressure for cuts
SPY/TLT color and rate-market behavior confirm the macro read

scoring.method: weighted vote-share over source direction, one vote per event cluster (no magnitude averaging)
scoring.clustering: one vote per event_key; representative = max-weight source; keyless sources are singleton clusters

sources.title: Why a CPI surprise could trip up the Fed's rate-cutting plans
sources.evidence_text: The article says an upside CPI surprise could push the Fed toward a pause in rate cuts and keep the policy rate unchanged at the next meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: If inflation surprises higher, the Fed is more likely to delay easing to preserve credibility on price stability.

sources.title: Inflation edges up, highlighting Fed's bumpy path to stable prices
sources.evidence_text: The article says October CPI rose to 2.6% year over year, which it described as a bump that still likely would not change the Fed's near-term course.
sources.why_it_matters: A firmer inflation print reduces the Fed's room to cut aggressively even if it does not fully reverse the easing cycle.

sources.title: Lower-Than-Expected Inflation Keeps Fed On Track For October Rate Cut
sources.evidence_text: The piece says September CPI rose more slowly than expected and kept the Fed on track to cut rates in October.
sources.why_it_matters: When inflation undershoots forecasts, the Fed has more room to ease without appearing to risk reaccelerating prices.

sources.title: Tame US inflation gives the Fed room for more rate cuts
sources.evidence_text: ING argued that softer November inflation gave the Fed more room to deliver additional cuts in 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: A clear disinflation surprise eases the constraint on the Fed's inflation mandate and supports more accommodation.

sources.title: CPI Surprises to the Downside
sources.evidence_text: The article says the latest CPI report came in well below expectations, which improved the odds of Fed rate cuts.
sources.why_it_matters: A softer inflation surprise reduces pressure on the Fed to keep policy restrictive and supports additional easing.

sources.title: Schedule of Selected Releases 2026
sources.evidence_text: BLS listed upcoming labor-market releases, including JOLTS on September 29 and the Employment Situation on October 2, 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: Upcoming official data can quickly shift the Fed reaction function if labor conditions weaken more than expected.

sources.title: CPI Home : U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics
sources.evidence_text: The BLS CPI home page shows August 2026 CPI at 0.4% month over month and 3.4% year over year.
sources.why_it_matters: The latest inflation print staying above target reduces the odds that the Fed will view policy as sufficiently disinflationary to justify faster easing.

sources.title: Federal Reserve Board - News & Events
sources.evidence_text: The Fed's news page lists the September 16 FOMC statement release as a major policy event.
sources.why_it_matters: The release anchors the latest official policy decision that markets and the Fed reaction function will use as the starting point for expectations.

sources.title: September Fed Meeting: Live Updates and Commentary
sources.evidence_text: The article says futures were pricing a high probability of a 25-basis-point hike at the September 15–16, 2026 FOMC meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: Market pricing that shifts toward hikes or away from cuts signals that incoming data are being read as less consistent with continued easing.

sources.title: Fed Rate Probability | FOMC Meeting Odds & Rate Cut Forecast 2026
sources.evidence_text: The page showed a high implied probability of a 25 basis point hike for the next meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: A strong hike probability implies the market expects tighter policy rather than renewed easing.

sources.title: Treasury, 2-Year - Economic Data Series
sources.evidence_text: FRED’s Treasury 2-Year tag shows daily data available through September 14, 2026, confirming the series is current and recently updated.
sources.why_it_matters: Current market data are essential for assessing whether investors are repricing the Fed toward fewer cuts or a higher-for-longer stance.

sources.title: Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC raised the federal funds target range by 25 basis points and said job gains have kept pace with the workforce while unemployment has changed little.
sources.why_it_matters: A rate hike and language describing labor conditions as solid indicate the Fed sees little need to ease policy for labor-market support.

sources.title: Federal Reserve Board and FOMC release economic projections from the September 15-16 FOMC meeting
sources.evidence_text: The September projections showed the median fed funds rate path above the current target range for later 2026 and 2027, implying no near-term easing bias.
sources.why_it_matters: A higher projected rate path means policy makers see less room to cut without a meaningful slowdown in inflation or labor-market conditions.

sources.title: September 16, 2026: FOMC Projections materials, accessible version
sources.evidence_text: The September projections showed the unemployment rate at 4.1% in 2026 and a relatively stable path thereafter.
sources.why_it_matters: A stable unemployment outlook reduces pressure for near-term easing because the labor market is not deteriorating.

sources.title: US weekly jobless claims unexpectedly fall
sources.evidence_text: The report says initial jobless claims fell to 196,000 and continuing claims also dropped, pointing to a still-solid labor market.
sources.why_it_matters: Lower claims indicate limited labor-market deterioration, which argues against rapid additional easing and can support a tighter stance.

sources.title: US weekly jobless claims unexpectedly fall
sources.evidence_text: The report also noted that continuing claims fell to 1.730 million, a proxy for hiring that suggests some resilience in labor demand.
sources.why_it_matters: Resilient hiring reduces the odds that the Fed will need to front-load cuts to defend the labor market.

sources.title: Transcript of Chairman Warsh's Press Conference
sources.evidence_text: The Chair said job gains have kept pace with the workforce, unemployment is around 4.1%, and claims are consistent with full employment.
sources.why_it_matters: Fed communication describing labor markets as near full employment reduces the case for additional cuts on labor-market grounds.

sources.title: Producer Price Index up 5.4 percent for the 12 months ended August 2026
sources.evidence_text: Producer prices increased 5.4 percent over the 12 months ended August, with goods up 7.7 percent and services up 4.5 percent.
sources.why_it_matters: Stronger pipeline inflation raises the risk that consumer inflation stays sticky, which would keep the Fed cautious.

sources.title: Meeting calendars and information
sources.evidence_text: The Fed’s calendar shows the September 15-16 FOMC meeting and indicates minutes are scheduled for release on October 7, 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: The scheduled minutes release is the next official document that could refine the balance between inflation risk and labor-market slack.

sources.title: Fed raises rates in search of timelier drop in inflation, sees more hikes
sources.evidence_text: The Fed raised rates and signaled additional hikes ahead, indicating a more restrictive policy path.
sources.why_it_matters: Forward guidance of more hikes suggests the reaction function is reacting more to inflation persistence than to modest labor-market softening.

sources.title: Fed rate decision September 2026: Rates rise to 3.75%-4%
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to a 3.75% to 4.00% target range.
sources.why_it_matters: A hike signals that the Fed is prioritizing inflation control over labor-market easing, shifting policy toward tighter conditions.

sources.title: Fed rate tracker — live FOMC cut, hold & hike odds
sources.evidence_text: The tracker says the federal funds target range is 3.75% to 4.00% after the September 15 to 16 FOMC meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: Market-implied pricing helps gauge whether investors see the Fed as moving into or staying in a tighter policy setting.

sources.title: Federal Reserve Monetary Policy
sources.evidence_text: The Fed's policy page lists the FOMC minutes release for August 19, 2026, confirming a recent communications update on policy deliberations.
sources.why_it_matters: Recent FOMC communications are the clearest signal of how the Committee is balancing inflation against employment risks.

sources.title: H.15 - Selected Interest Rates (Daily) - September 17, 2026
sources.evidence_text: The Federal Reserve's H.15 series shows the 2-year Treasury yield rising to 4.85% on 2026-09-23 after trading at 4.67% on 2026-09-17.
sources.why_it_matters: A rising 2-year yield usually signals a higher expected path for the fed funds rate, which argues for fewer cuts or a tighter policy stance.

sources.title: Market Yield on U.S. Treasury Securities at 2-Year Constant Maturity, Quoted on an Investment Basis
sources.evidence_text: FRED's 2-year Treasury series was 4.85% on 2026-09-23, up from 4.71% on 2026-09-22 and 4.67% on 2026-09-17.
sources.why_it_matters: The 2-year yield is a close proxy for the market's expected average policy rate over the near term, so a higher reading implies less easing priced in.

sources.title: Treasury yields move higher as volatile week wraps up
sources.evidence_text: The story reported the 2-year Treasury yield gained to 4.76% as the week ended.
sources.why_it_matters: A rising 2-year yield after the policy decision suggests markets are leaning toward a tighter expected Fed path.

sources.title: The Fed - September 15-16, 2026 FOMC Meeting
sources.evidence_text: The meeting page links the statement, implementation note, and press conference for the September 15-16 FOMC meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: This is the official package that conveys the Committee's latest assessment of inflation and labor-market conditions.

sources.title: VIEW Stocks pull back after Fed raises rates, points to another hike ...
sources.evidence_text: Reuters reported that the 2-year yield rose after the Fed's latest move, while policy projections showed most officials expected at least one more quarter-point hike by year-end.
sources.why_it_matters: When short rates and Fed dots move higher together, markets and policymakers are both leaning toward fewer cuts or additional tightening.

sources.title: 2-year Treasury yield reaches multi-year high after Fed rate ...
sources.evidence_text: Coverage said the 2-year yield hit a multi-year high after the Fed's latest hike, reflecting expectations for additional policy tightening.
sources.why_it_matters: When the policy-sensitive front end rises after a Fed move, markets are usually reassessing the likely terminal rate and cutting back expected easing.

sources.title: Federal Reserve raises federal funds target range to 3.75 ...
sources.evidence_text: The article said the September median policy-rate projection sat above the new target midpoint, consistent with one more quarter-point hike.
sources.why_it_matters: A projected policy rate above the current midpoint implies the Fed is not yet ready to declare an easing cycle.

sources.title: FOMC - September 2026
sources.evidence_text: The summary says the FOMC raised its policy rate by 25 basis points and revised its unemployment and inflation projections upward and downward respectively.
sources.why_it_matters: A rate hike signals the Committee sees inflation persistence as the more important risk than labor-market cooling.

sources.title: The full statement from the Federal Reserve Board for September 2026
sources.evidence_text: The statement says the Committee raised the target range by 25 basis points, noted inflation remains elevated, and said the action supports a timely return to 2 percent.
sources.why_it_matters: An actual hike with explicit inflation concern is the clearest signal that policy is drifting toward tightening rather than easing.

sources.title: News Release: Employment and Training Administration — Initial Claims for Unemployment Insurance
sources.evidence_text: Seasonally adjusted initial jobless claims fell by 10,000 to 196,000 in the week ending September 12, with the four-week average also declining.
sources.why_it_matters: Lower claims point to a still-resilient labor market, but the trend can still support cuts if disinflation continues and labor slack does not reaccelerate.

sources.title: US Fed Funds Interest Rate: Latest Updates and Trends
sources.evidence_text: The page reports a 73.5% implied probability of another 25 basis point rate increase at the next meeting as of September 24, 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: Market pricing for another hike suggests investors see the Fed reaction function leaning against easing and toward further tightening.

sources.title: September 2026 FOMC rate decision
sources.evidence_text: The FOMC raised the target range for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 3.75% to 4.00%.
sources.why_it_matters: An actual hike is the clearest signal that the Fed judged inflation or labor-market risks to outweigh easing conditions.

sources.title: FOMC Statement: September 2026
sources.evidence_text: The note says the Fed described activity as expanding at a solid pace and said job gains have kept pace with the workforce while unemployment changed little.
sources.why_it_matters: If the Fed characterizes labor conditions as stable rather than weakening, it is less likely to justify aggressive easing.

sources.title: FOMC Meeting Highlights: Fed Signals Another Hike In 2026
sources.evidence_text: The article said CME FedWatch showed more than a 90% probability of a quarter-point hike heading into the meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: Heavy pricing of a hike implies markets were already moving away from cuts in response to inflation risk.

sources.title: Implementation Note issued September 16, 2026
sources.evidence_text: The Board raised interest on reserve balances to 3.90% and increased the primary credit rate to 4.0% effective September 17, 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: Higher administered rates reinforce tighter financial conditions and constrain the scope for easier policy transmission.

sources.title: CME FedWatch Tool
sources.evidence_text: Fed funds futures and options pricing on the next FOMC meeting are designed to show the market-implied odds of a cut, hold, or hike.
sources.why_it_matters: Market-implied probabilities summarize whether financial conditions are pricing easier or tighter policy at the next decision.

sources.title: Two-year U.S. Treasury yield reaches new multi-year high
sources.evidence_text: The 2-year Treasury yield touched 4.744%, its highest intraday level since July 2024, alongside CME FedWatch showing a 58% chance of another rate increase in October.
sources.why_it_matters: A higher front-end yield plus hike odds suggests the market expects fewer cuts and potentially more tightening from the Fed.

sources.title: Two-year yield at highest since 2024 after Fed hikes rates
sources.evidence_text: The 2-year Treasury yield hit 4.744% after the Fed’s rate hike, which the article described as the yield’s highest level since July 2024.
sources.why_it_matters: The 2-year yield is closely tied to expected policy rates, so a move to multi-year highs points to tighter policy expectations.

sources.title: Fed's Interest Rate Decision: September 16, 2026
sources.evidence_text: The summary says the Fed raised rates to 3.75%–4.00% after a stretch of holding steady and described the move as a continuation of a restrictive stance.
sources.why_it_matters: A tighter starting point reduces the odds that the next move is a cut unless inflation and activity soften materially.

sources.title: 2026-09-21, Selected Interest Rates Instruments, Yields in ...
sources.evidence_text: The FRED release table lists the 2-year Treasury yield at 4.85% on 2026-09-23 within the selected interest rates set.
sources.why_it_matters: This corroborates that the front end of the Treasury curve is pricing a relatively restrictive policy path.

sources.title: US jobless claims fall to 196,000 during holiday week
sources.evidence_text: Weekly claims declined by 10,000 to 196,000 in the week ended September 12, with the release describing the reading as among the lowest since 1969.
sources.why_it_matters: A resilient claims series argues against near-term tightening in policy support, but it also weakens the case for immediate cuts.

sources.title: September 2026 FOMC Recap
sources.evidence_text: The recap says the September meeting delivered the first Fed hike since 2023 and reflected concern about persistently elevated inflation.
sources.why_it_matters: A first hike after a long pause indicates the Fed is still willing to tighten if inflation risks dominate labor-market softness.

sources.title: CME FedWatch sees 90.4% chance of a September Fed rate hike after August CPI
sources.evidence_text: FedWatch-implied probabilities jumped to about a 90.4% chance of a 25-basis-point hike after the August CPI release.
sources.why_it_matters: When markets price a hike rather than cuts, financial conditions and expectations move in a tighter direction.

sources.title: Latest Numbers : U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics
sources.evidence_text: The BLS latest numbers page shows core CPI at 2.4% year over year in August 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: Core inflation above 2% suggests underlying price pressures remain inconsistent with a quick return to easier policy.

sources.title: Fed policymakers forecast one more rate hike this year
sources.evidence_text: Coverage of the SEP said policymakers now expect higher inflation this year and beyond, reinforcing a less dovish path.
sources.why_it_matters: If officials are marking up inflation forecasts, the reaction function generally shifts toward holding rates higher for longer.

sources.title: Fed Hikes in 12-0 Vote, Commits to Inflation Fight
sources.evidence_text: The commentary highlighted that the Fed marked up 2026 headline and core PCE inflation forecasts versus June.
sources.why_it_matters: Upward inflation revisions make the Fed less likely to justify cuts on a disinflationary basis.

sources.title: Fed Outlook 2026: Rate forecasts and fixed income strategies
sources.evidence_text: The piece says markets have shifted from expecting cuts to pricing in the possibility of additional hikes as inflation remains above target.
sources.why_it_matters: If inflation stays sticky, the Fed's reaction function shifts toward restraint, making cuts less likely and hikes more plausible.

sources.title: 2026 Speeches
sources.evidence_text: The Fed's speeches index shows a new September 23 speech titled A Long-Term View on the Costs of Shelter.
sources.why_it_matters: A fresh speech on shelter costs may signal continued attention to inflation composition, but the index alone does not reveal policy direction.

sources.title: FOMC Summary of Economic Projections, September 2026
sources.evidence_text: The median FOMC participant projected core PCE inflation at 3.4% in 2026 and unemployment at 4.1% through 2029.
sources.why_it_matters: Inflation staying above target in the SEP argues for holding policy restrictive rather than rapidly easing.

sources.title: Treasury yields are little changed as traders await Fed comments
sources.evidence_text: The 2-year Treasury yield was reported at 4.743% on September 22 while traders waited for Fed commentary.
sources.why_it_matters: A still-elevated front-end yield suggests the market expects policy to remain restrictive, limiting the case for imminent cuts.

sources.title: U.S. Treasury Investors Flock to 2-Year Notes as Yields Near 4.75%, Seen Overpricing Further Fed Tightening
sources.evidence_text: The article says some investors think the 2-year note is already pricing in most of the Fed's further tightening outlook.
sources.why_it_matters: If the front end has already priced in much of the hiking path, the Fed may see less market support for an easing pivot.

sources.title: CME FedWatch: 86% Chance of a 25 bp Fed Rate Hike at ...
sources.evidence_text: The piece reports CME FedWatch odds in the mid-80% range for a 25 bp hike at the September FOMC meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: When futures assign most weight to a hike, the market is pricing a more restrictive policy path than cuts.

sources.title: FOMC September 2026 Odds for a Rate Hike Surpass 50%
sources.evidence_text: The article says traders using CME FedWatch assigned nearly a 56% chance of a quarter-point hike at the September FOMC meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: Market pricing above 50% for a hike indicates the balance of expected policy outcomes has shifted away from cuts.

sources.title: Fed rate hike Sept 16, 2026: 3.75%-4.00%, One More Coming
sources.evidence_text: The article reports that the Fed raised the target range by 25 bp on September 16, 2026 and that the new projections point to one more quarter-point move by December.
sources.why_it_matters: An actual hike and a projected additional increase both argue for a tightening regime rather than an easing one.

sources.title: 2-Year Treasury Yield Hits 4.76%, Pricing Out Fed Rate Cuts
sources.evidence_text: The 2-year Treasury yield is reported at 4.76%, its highest reading in the recent range, and the note says the front end is pricing out rate cuts quickly.
sources.why_it_matters: A higher 2-year yield usually signals markets expect a less dovish Fed, which raises the bar for near-term easing.

sources.title: CME FedWatch Prices in 88.7% Chance of 25-Basis-Point ...
sources.evidence_text: Fed funds futures were summarized as giving an 88.7% probability of a 25 bp Fed rate hike at the September FOMC meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: Fed funds futures directly encode the market’s expected policy path, so a high hike probability points to tightening expectations.

sources.title: Fed rate decision: markets price 25-bp hike ahead of FOMC, sources say
sources.evidence_text: The piece says markets were pricing roughly a 25 bp hike at the September FOMC meeting and notes the 10-year yield rose above 5% intraday.
sources.why_it_matters: Rising long-end yields alongside hike pricing reinforce a market view that policy will stay tighter for longer.

sources.title: Current Employment Statistics - CES (National)
sources.evidence_text: The CES page continues to show August payroll growth of 162,000 and notes the September employment report is scheduled for October 2, 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: The latest official payroll reading still looks firm, but no newer release is available to change the Fed's near-term labor assessment.

sources.title: US labor market: Defensive stability in a low-hire, low-fire ...
sources.evidence_text: The piece says weekly initial claims have hovered near 200,000 through 2026, indicating a still-subdued layoff environment.
sources.why_it_matters: Subdued layoffs reduce the urgency for Fed tightening and keep the door open to cuts if inflation eases further.

sources.title: Warsh says US economy has strengthened, inflation is the problem
sources.evidence_text: The Fed chair said the labor market is essentially at full employment while inflation has shown little improvement.
sources.why_it_matters: If labor remains at full employment, the Fed has more room to keep policy tight while prioritizing inflation control.

sources.title: Fed hikes, hints at more: 7 takeaways from the September FOMC
sources.evidence_text: Market commentary on the meeting emphasized that job gains are keeping pace with workforce growth and that the Fed left the labor-market language largely unchanged.
sources.why_it_matters: Stable labor-market language alongside a hike suggests the Fed does not yet see enough weakening to justify easing.

sources.title: Federal Reserve Monetary Policy
sources.evidence_text: The piece said market prices and the median Fed projection pointed to another rate increase in 2026 and additional hikes by mid-2027.
sources.why_it_matters: A market path centered on further hikes implies little room for cuts in the near term.

sources.title: FRED Blog - September 2026
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
sources.evidence_text: The blog summarizes the median FOMC projection as 3.4% core PCE inflation in 2026, with a return to the 2% target only by 2029.
sources.why_it_matters: A slower path back to target supports a more restrictive stance than markets may price.

sources.title: Fed review The hike was expected The message was more hawkish
sources.evidence_text: Market commentary said the Fed funds path repriced higher after the September meeting, with fewer cuts and more hikes embedded in the curve.
sources.why_it_matters: A higher terminal-rate path in market pricing signals that traders think the inflation surprise has reduced the odds of near-term easing.

sources.title: U.S. Treasury yields ease as investors await fresh jobs data
sources.evidence_text: The 2-year Treasury yield was reported near 4.74% to 4.77% on 2026-09-22 as traders waited for fresh labor-market data.
sources.why_it_matters: Near-term policy pricing can move with incoming jobs data, which the Fed watches closely for signs of labor-market slack or resilience.

sources.title: Selected Interest Rates (Daily) - H.15 - Federal Reserve Board
sources.evidence_text: The effective federal funds rate was 3.88% on September 22, 2026, remaining above the prior week's level after the September FOMC meeting.
sources.why_it_matters: A firmer effective rate signals the market is still pricing and operating at a restrictive policy level, which reduces the room for near-term cuts.

sources.title: Effr
sources.evidence_text: FRED shows the effective federal funds rate at 3.88% on September 22, 2026, with the next release date listed for September 24, 2026.
sources.why_it_matters: The current policy rate anchors the OIS and futures path, so a stable rate keeps the near-term reaction function focused on incoming data rather than an active easing cycle.

sources.title: US Labor Market Snapshot — September 2026
sources.evidence_text: The snapshot says posted wages rose 2.5% over the year ending August 2026 and the unemployment rate held at 4.1% in July.
sources.why_it_matters: Slower wage growth can ease inflation pressure, which supports the Fed's ability to keep policy easier if labor demand is not reaccelerating.

sources.title: US weekly jobless claims decrease as labor market regains footing
sources.evidence_text: Initial claims slipped to 197,000 in the week ended September 19, while continuing claims rose slightly to 1.719 million.
sources.why_it_matters: Low initial claims argue against a rapidly cooling labor market, though a small rise in continuing claims keeps recession risk on the radar.

sources.title: Summary of Economic Projections, September 16, 2026
sources.evidence_text: The SEP shows inflation remaining above the Fed's target through 2028 and converging only gradually over the forecast horizon.
sources.why_it_matters: A slower return to target reduces room for easing because the Fed prioritizes restoring inflation to 2% sustainably.

sources.title: New York Fed DSGE Model Forecast—September 2026
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
sources.evidence_text: The New York Fed model forecast still showed core PCE inflation above target in 2026 and only gradually easing toward 2% later in the horizon.
sources.why_it_matters: A slow, model-based decline in core inflation supports caution on cuts, but it is less binding than realized data.

sources.title: Why Hike | Tom Barkin | Inflation | Employment
sources.evidence_text: Barkin said the risks to inflation outweigh the risks to maximum employment and noted unemployment remained at 4.1 percent.
sources.why_it_matters: When a Fed official prioritizes inflation over labor-market risk, the reaction function leans toward fewer cuts or additional restraint.

sources.title: Federal Reserve Board - 2026 Speeches
sources.evidence_text: The Fed’s speeches index shows a September 23 entry titled A Long-Term View on the Costs of Shelter.
sources.why_it_matters: A new speech topic on shelter costs can matter for inflation persistence, but the index alone does not reveal a policy shift.

sources.title: Federal Reserve recent postings
sources.evidence_text: The Fed posted the September 15-16 FOMC economic projections shortly after the meeting, reinforcing that the latest policy update is the main guide for the next decision.
sources.why_it_matters: The latest projection set is the clearest read on the Fed's reaction function until fresh labor and inflation data arrive.
